diagnosis_from_existing_data.source: plan-v8 blind rows (v7-full controllers, bench9) and v9 training/selection logs; no v9 blind data used
findings: dash: SNN + ES reaches the target ~30% sooner than the classical opponent (t_reach 0.54-0.67 s vs 0.86 s) but brakes worse: roll-class overshoot 0.10-0.17 m vs 0.04 m, longer settling; roll-class dash ratio 1.0-1.5 is where SNN loses
redirect: overrun 0.11-0.14 m vs 0.09 m (braking again)
pitch/diag dash: no controller meets the settle criterion (0/48 cases each) -> constant 4 s term compresses the dash ratio toward 1; NOT changed in v10 (scoring kept identical to v9)
v8 crashes: 5 tilt + 5 upward height escapes; the network has no height input
v9 selection, seed 1: validation objective 1.005 (gen 9) -> the selection-to-blind gap of v7/v8 (+0.05..0.10) makes 0.95 hard to reach without a real gain
diagnosis_from_existing_data.hypothesis: the classical schedule brakes on a timer and the PID sees height; the learned layer has neither a notion of time since the command (LIF/delay memory spans tens of ms) nor height. Giving it phasic (adapting) command copies and height channels should reduce overshoot/overrun and height escapes.
